knowledge_base.content: I am TK-Bot, Tarun Karnati's personal AI assistant. I provide fast, friendly, and confident information about his background, projects, skills, and achievements to recruiters and visitors. My responses are based on verified professional data about Tarun.
I represent Tarun in a professional yet approachable tone — confident, technically sharp, and easy to talk to. My goal is to make every conversation feel natural, useful, and insightful.

The best way to contact Tarun is by email at tarunk1109@gmail.com or by phone at +1 (647) 883-2660. You can also connect with him on LinkedIn at https://linkedin.com/in/tarunkarnati and view his work on GitHub at https://github.com/Tarunk1109. His portfolio is live at https://tarunk1109.github.io/portfolio_ai/.
A downloadable PDF of Tarun's resume is available directly on his portfolio website. You can find the link on the main page.
His long-term vision is to grow into a Lead Software Engineer or Solutions Architect — building intelligent systems that merge full-stack development, cloud architecture, and applied AI.
Tarun is fully authorized to work in Canada and is open to both co-op and full-time opportunities.
His main domains of interest include Full-Stack Web Development, Generative AI, MCP and LLM Integration, Cloud Platforms (Azure, AWS), DevOps Automation, and Intelligent Systems.

Tarun has a publication titled 'Public Relationships Using NLP and Machine Learning' published in the International Journal of Creative Research Thoughts (IJCRT), 2024. The paper leverages Logistic Regression and Naive Bayes to analyze online product reviews and extract customer sentiment. Link: http://ijcrt.org/viewfull.php?&p_id=IJCRT2405210.

Tarun holds multiple certifications: 1) Introduction to Model Context Protocol — Anthropic, 2) Microsoft AZ-900: Azure Fundamentals — Microsoft, 3) Generative AI: Working with Large Language Models — NASBA and LinkedIn Learning, 4) Docker Foundations Professional Certificate — LinkedIn Learning & Docker, 5) Career Essentials in Software Development — Microsoft and LinkedIn Learning.

Tarun's key strengths include strong analytical thinking, adaptability, and a deep interest in AI-driven innovation. He is highly collaborative, quick to learn new technologies, and excels at breaking down complex problems into clear, efficient solutions.

Tarun values simplicity, precision, and progress. His personal motto is 'Build. Learn. Improve.' He believes that great code should not just work — it should teach you something new every time you write it.
Tarun communicates clearly, works effectively in teams, and maintains a proactive attitude in problem-solving. His curiosity and attention to detail make him a dependable and innovative developer.

Tarun's portfolio website showcases his personality and technical skills. It includes light/dark mode, smooth animations, and TK-Bot — an interactive AI chatbot that provides information about him to visitors and recruiters. Live at https://tarunk1109.github.io/portfolio_ai/.
Beyond tech, Tarun enjoys fitness, outdoor sports, and exploring emerging technologies. He believes that balancing physical and mental activity keeps creativity sharp.

Tarun envisions building AI-powered platforms that improve daily life — combining full-stack systems, intelligent automation, MCP orchestration, and cloud technology to create user-focused digital experiences.

Tarun’s documented projects are: EvenHub Edu, BakeOps, SENTINEL, Compass, AutoApply, MedSafe, FactoryVision, ContextOS, Speech Emotion Recognition, Jetson / Edge AI, SubGenie, FATHOM, AEOscope, ORCA AI, PerkPal, Alberta AI Gateway, Sentiment Analysis / NLP Research.

Tarun Karnati is a Toronto-based software and AI engineer, a recent Humber Information Technology Solutions graduate, and a four-time hackathon award recipient. His relevant experience includes a sponsor-supported academic capstone, not salaried software employment.

Completed postgraduate studies in Information Technology Solutions at Humber Polytechnic, January 2025–August 2026; bachelor’s degree in Data Science at SRK Institute of Technology, 2020–2024. Dean’s Honour List for all four Humber semesters, as confirmed by Tarun.

BakeOps: second place, TMLS × FGF Brands Agentic Hackathon 2026. SENTINEL: Track 1 winner, Agnic.AI Agentic Commerce Pioneers 2026. FATHOM: second prize, MyChoice Ontario All-Quote Agent Challenge 2026. Alberta AI Gateway: second place, Brainstem Alliance Hackathon 2025. These are four awards, not four overall first-place wins.

EvenHub Edu. A school-management platform with an AI assistant for parents, teachers, and administrators. Connects school documents, events, menus, and lunch orders in one portal. Status: Sponsor-supported capstone. Stack: React, Node.js, Firebase, Gemini, Cloud Run. Led a four-person Humber capstone for an external sponsor, delivered May–August 2026. Expanded a working sponsor prototype into a platform used by real people. Implemented document extraction, chunking, embedding retrieval, semantic reranking, role-aware context, and streamed answers. Read-only Gmail integration and tools connect the assistant to school workflows.

BakeOps. An AI command center for bakery operations. Routes equipment, supply-chain, and recipe scenarios to specialist agents and brings their recommendations into a live dashboard. Status: Hackathon prototype. Stack: Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, Claude. Built with Nanditha for the TMLS × FGF Brands Agentic Hackathon; second place in 2026. An orchestrator selects three specialists, runs selected work in parallel, then synthesizes the results. Includes SSE updates, label analysis, Open Food Facts, and Telegram alerts. Factory scenarios and dashboard telemetry are simulated; displayed savings are demonstration estimates. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/BakeOps

SENTINEL. A commerce assistant that turns requests and photos into evidence-backed product shortlists and live merchant quotes. A separate sandbox flow demonstrates checkout with explicit approval. Status: Commerce demo. Stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, OpenAI, Agnic. Track 1 winner at Agnic.AI Agentic Commerce Pioneers 2026. Supports product requests, broken-part inspection, and reference-photo bills of materials. Server-side checks verify merchants, quotes, consent, and provider order status. Real-money purchasing is disabled. Checkout demonstrations use the payment provider’s sandbox; scheduling is runtime-only. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/Sentinel https://sentinel-taupe-two.vercel.app

Compass. A Slack copilot for developer questions about microservices. Retrieves from OpenAPI specifications and documentation, cites its sources, and traces service dependencies. Status: Proof of concept. Stack: Python, LangGraph, Qdrant, Cohere, Slack. Combines dense retrieval with BM25, reciprocal-rank fusion, and reranking. Keeps API operations intact and uses dependency metadata for impact questions. Demonstrated against 12 synthetic payment-domain services. Conversation memory is in-process, and the current interface supports direct messages. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/compass-slack

AutoApply. A job-discovery pipeline that collects listings, removes duplicates, applies practical filters, and ranks relevant opportunities with short AI explanations. Status: Local tool. Stack: Python, Claude, Firestore, pytest. Integrates Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby listings. Applies cheap filters before model scoring, isolates adapter failures, and writes ranked results in batches. Working local pipeline with a console digest. It discovers and ranks jobs; it does not submit applications. Email delivery and scheduled cloud execution are not completed.

MedSafe. A medication-interaction explorer that combines a drug knowledge graph with a web interface to help users inspect relationships between medications. Status: Academic project. Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Neo4j, PostgreSQL, GraphQL. Built with React, Neo4j Aura, Neon PostgreSQL, Prisma, and GraphQL Yoga. Includes authentication and AI integrations for explanations and image-based input. Academic software demonstration using interaction data. It is not clinically validated and should not be used to make treatment decisions.  https://medsafe-graph.vercel.app

FactoryVision. An image-quality inspection backend that connects a C# API to a Python vision service. Validates uploads, analyses visual quality, and stores inspection history. Status: API prototype. Stack: C# / .NET, FastAPI, OpenCV, SQLite, Docker. ASP.NET Core uses dependency injection and a configurable inference provider; EF Core persists metadata in SQLite. Includes Swagger, structured errors, xUnit, and pytest coverage. OpenCV measures brightness, contrast, and blur. This is a prototype heuristic, not a trained manufacturing-defect detector or a live factory integration. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/factoryvision-ai-api

ContextOS. A memory-management layer for long-running LLM conversations. Keeps recent turns in hot memory, compresses older turns into summaries, and archives the original text. Status: Local prototype. Stack: Python, Claude, tiktoken, Streamlit. Tracks token usage and session cost, compresses older messages with Haiku, and displays memory state in a Streamlit dashboard. The completed core uses a file-based state exchange. Semantic cold-memory retrieval, checkpoint restoration, and RAG features are roadmap items. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/ContextOS

Speech Emotion Recognition. An audio classifier for eight emotions. Compares an ANN, CNN, and CNN–Transformer, then averages their predictions in an ensemble with a Streamlit demo. Status: Academic ML project. Stack: Python, TensorFlow, Librosa, scikit-learn, Streamlit. Uses 4,240 RAVDESS and TESS speech clips, MFCC features, and Mel-spectrograms. A four-person academic submission with CNN implementation and project coordination among Tarun’s contributions. The project report records 92.3% ensemble accuracy on an 848-clip held-out test set. This is a clip-level split on acted speech; speaker-disjoint evaluation is not established. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/speech-emotion-recognition

Jetson / Edge AI. An object-detection pipeline exploring accelerated inference on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, bringing computer-vision workloads onto an edge device. Status: Edge-inference project. Stack: YOLOv8, PyTorch, ONNX, TensorRT, OpenCV. Uses model export and TensorRT FP16 optimisation, with Flask for a lightweight application interface. Focuses on deployment and inference acceleration. Hardware benchmark conditions are not documented here, so no throughput or latency claim is presented.

SubGenie. A subscription manager that tracks recurring costs and usage, calculates cost per use, and offers AI suggestions for cutting underused services or finding alternatives. Status: Academic web application. Stack: Node.js, Express, MongoDB, EJS, OpenAI. Includes authenticated subscription management, usage logs, analytics, and an AI advisor. A natural-language Telegram bot supports everyday tracking and reminders. MongoDB and Mongoose store user-scoped data; JWT and bcrypt support authentication. The interface uses server-rendered EJS, Tailwind, and Chart.js. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/Subgenie

FATHOM. An evidence-first browser automation tool for researching Ontario auto-insurance journeys. Records observations and blocked steps through a deterministic action-policy gate. Status: Challenge prototype. Stack: Browser automation, Policy engine, Evidence logging. Second prize at the MyChoice Ontario All-Quote Agent Challenge 2026. Captures timestamped, redacted evidence and distinguishes refusals from unresolved attempts. No real insurer returned a price under the hypothetical profile in this build. Comparable price examples come from a labelled local sandbox; the tool does not purchase policies. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/fathom

AEOscope. A website auditor for SEO and answer-engine readiness. Checks page structure, schema, and content clarity, then uses Claude to identify information gaps in a brand’s website. Status: CLI tool. Stack: Python, BeautifulSoup, Claude, Rich. Produces SEO and AEO scores, prioritised recommendations, and Markdown or JSON reports. A no-AI mode runs the rule-based checks without an API key. The AI perception report is a simulation based on supplied website content; it does not measure rankings or directly query every search engine. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/AEOscope

ORCA AI. A prompt-to-web-app workflow that generates code, writes project files, pushes to GitHub, deploys through Railway, and validates the result with a browser. Status: Development prototype. Stack: Python, Flask, Socket.IO, Playwright, Railway. Uses multiple AI providers with ordered fallback, an in-process event queue, and a dashboard for build stages and logs. A failed build can trigger one AI repair attempt. Tool adapters coordinate browser, GitHub, shell, and deployment work; this does not imply a production-grade recovery system. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/orca_ai

PerkPal. A community-focused deals platform for discovering relevant offers by audience and category, with registration, login, personalised offer pages, and a wishlist interface. Status: Web application project. Stack: HTML / CSS, JavaScript, Spring Boot, MongoDB. Static frontend pages organise offers for students, seniors, and other communities. The personalised flow connects to a separate local backend API. Built as a web-development project. The public frontend repository is not a complete hosted full-stack service. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/PerkPal

Alberta AI Gateway. An AI-assisted tourism and travel platform for Alberta. Combines trip planning, conversational help, speech features, local events and weather, and interactive 3D content. Status: Hackathon project. Stack: React, Node.js, MongoDB, Whisper, Gemini. Second place at the Brainstem Alliance Hackathon 2025; built and led during a three-day sprint. React frontend and Express API integrate OpenAI, Gemini, Ticketmaster, and OpenWeather. JWT authentication and MongoDB support accounts and saved itineraries. https://github.com/Tarunk1109/alberta-ai-gateway https://alberta-ai-gateway.vercel.app/

Sentiment Analysis / NLP Research. A product-review sentiment-classification study using Logistic Regression and Naive Bayes, published as “Public Relationships using NLP and Machine Learning.” Status: Published academic work. Stack: Python, scikit-learn, NLP. Published in IJCRT, volume 12, issue 5, May 2024. Tarun is a co-author of the academic paper. Explores classical machine-learning approaches to review classification. The paper link provides the research context and reported findings.  https://ijcrt.org/viewfull.php?p_id=IJCRT2405210
